newsitem.title: UK: Legal & General at new high on bid hopes.
newsitem.headline: Legal & General at new high on bid hopes.

text.p: Shares in insurance group Legal & General Plc hit a record high on Monday, extending recent gains on a combination of bid speculation and dividend hopes, traders and analysts said.
The stock was up 14-1/2p at 806 by 1128 GMT, surpassing the previous peak of 802p set September 25 and continuing a surge since the end of June when it finished the month at 669p.

"There are still some short positions out there and the stock has a lot of momentum," said one trader. "And on fundamentals it doesn't look too expensive, trading at a premium of about 7-1/2 percent to book value."
Traders and analysts pointed to a string of recent developments in the insurance and banking sectors as having helped stoked bid speculation around Legal & General.

After Lloyds TSB Plc moved to mop up outstanding shares in Lloyds Abbey Life, NatWest Bank Plc securitised a $5 billion portfolio of business loans -- sparking speculation about how it intended to use the extra funds.

Separately Refuge Group Plc said today it added a new security to be issued to shareholders under the terms of its planned merger with United Friendly Plc -- highlighting the possible value of insurance companies' investment funds.

Michael Lindsay, analyst at Lehman Brothers, said the strength of Legal & General shares reflected continued bid speculation about the company as the insurance sector consolidated -- as well as L&G's stong dividend prospects.
"The management is committed to strong dividend growth and they can afford to pay, so it is a pretty strong story," Lindsay said.

"But we would consider the shares to be pretty high now. The shares are discounting a lot of good news, but while they have got these speculative factors driving them they are not going to be sold very strongly," he added.
